speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your gums or other mucous membranes, and small red spots on your skin called petechiae. To understand the cause, have you noticed any easy bruising, or do you or your family have a history of bleeding disorders?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP). Given the 4-year-old age, isolated mucocutaneous bleeding (epistaxis, gum bleeding, petechiae, bruising), and absence of fever or severe systemic symptoms in the history, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of ITP. No further diagnostic questions or tests are required to proceed with this management plan.
